A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TRACE study and contain readable main text, figures, tables, and Appendices A–J. Content can be matched reliably across pagination changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original RL training and hacking-detection experiments on math and coding tasks, including appendix analyses of hint complexity, monitor scale, and GRPO.

after.justification: v4 retains the original training, detection, loophole-discovery, and appendix experimental results.

M1.justification: v4 explicitly assigns coding RM exploits a score of 1, whereas v1's Section 4 footnote specifies the test-pass fraction. Both otherwise describe the same loophole-aware TRACE procedure. The PDFs do not resolve whether this reflects a method change or correction of incomplete documentation.

E1.justification: Both use Big-Math-Verified and APPS with the same in-context and reward-model loopholes, full and partial loophole settings, and appendix hint-complexity scenarios. No additional dataset, language, or task is evaluated.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparators remain unchanged: Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct monitoring for math, 32B for code, and the same monitor sizes in Appendices A–B. Newly cited approaches are not evaluated as baselines.

E3.justification: Section 4's coding-score specification changes from the fraction of tests passed to that fraction or 1 when the RM loophole is exploited. This is a limited reported scoring-protocol revision, without evidence of rerunning experiments. Splits, training settings, sampling temperatures, and detection thresholds remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The counterfactual checks, loophole-discovery case study, hint-complexity analysis, monitor scaling, truncation examples, and GRPO analyses are retained. The new overthinking discussion proposes future calibration but supplies no additional robustness experiment.

E5.justification: Existing shaded plots and sampling information are retained without new uncertainty definitions, repeated-run reporting, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Appendix I's clustering initialization count and seed also remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Matched figures retain their numerical results and qualitative findings. For example, Qwen2.5-3B IC detection remains 0.932 versus 0.660 F1 for TRACE and monitoring in math, and 0.587 versus 0.050 in code. Appendix results are also retained; revised labels do not introduce new outcomes.

T1.justification: The proxy-versus-true-reward distinction and AUC construction already appear in v1. v4's expected-proxy-reward notation makes that interpretation explicit without adding a substantive formal derivation, assumption, theorem, or proof.

C1.justification: Both claim that TRACE detects implicit reward hacking, outperforms CoT monitors, and supports unsupervised loophole discovery. The headline performance claims and demonstrated scope remain unchanged; reward-based wording clarifies the existing contribution.

C2.justification: Section 7 adds overthinking as a source of elevated TRACE scores without hacking and proposes calibration using clean questions. It also explicitly characterizes TRACE as a relative-effort proxy and discusses alternative internal-effort measures. These substantive qualifications remain untested.

D1.justification: v4 explicitly documents binary math rewards and coding RM-exploit score handling. Appendix F's training configurations and Appendices G–I's prompts and clustering instructions remain unchanged, with no new code or data access information.

R1.justification: v4 adds references to Liu et al. on multilingual hidden reasoning, Zhang et al. on internal correctness beliefs, Chen et al. on deep-thinking tokens, and Zhong et al.'s Hodoscope. These extend contextual discussion without substantially changing the paper's research positioning.

P1.justification: Localized rewrites replace verifier-passing or accuracy language with expected proxy reward, add two discussion paragraphs, and give the conclusion a separate heading. Author information and conference headers are updated, while the overall narrative and appendix organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Figures 5 and 19 adopt expected-reward labels, Figure 8 labels its AUC axis as TRACE score, and Figure 21's caption changes from average TRACE score to average test pass rate. Figures and tables are retained, with limited layout reflow and added conference headers.

improvement.justification: v4 improves clarity by distinguishing proxy reward from task correctness and acknowledging overthinking as a potential detection confound in Section 7. These are useful specification and interpretation improvements, but empirical evidence remains unchanged, the coding implementation change is unresolved, and the proposed calibration is not evaluated.
